strings: Pie for Billy is an errand caught in the crossfire of the longstanding feud between Elwynn Forest's Stonefield and Maclure families. Young Billy Maclure refuses to give up information regarding Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace without a pork belly pie in exchange. Adventurers must hunt local boars to gather meat for Bernice to bake the demanded bribe.

When approached regarding the theft of Auntie Bernice Stonefield's heirloom necklace, Billy Maclure exhibits none of the remorse an elder might hope for. Instead of returning the heirloom or confessing, the boy seizes an opportunity to indulge his appetite. He demands a freshly baked pork belly pie before he will utter a single word about who holds the necklace, knowing full well that Auntie Bernice is the finest cook in the valley.

The Maclures and Stonefields have traded insults, brawls, and accusations across the pumpkin patches for generations. Despite her deep indignation at feeding the rascal who stole her family jewelry, Auntie Bernice agrees to fire up her oven. In exchange for tender boar meat collected from the wild beasts roaming the adjacent pastures, she swallows her pride to appease the unruly youth and recover her prized possession.

Billy Maclure is an opportunistic farm boy using his knowledge of Auntie Bernice's stolen necklace as leverage. Knowing Bernice makes exceptional pork belly pies, he refuses to reveal who has the heirloom until his appetite is satisfied.

Having proven their basic tracking and stalking skills in the rolling hills of Mulgore, young tauren are directed outward into the arid wilderness of the Barrens. Melor Stonehoof sends aspiring hunters north of the border to report to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. This journey marks the hunter's formal transition from local trials to the demanding predatory hierarchy of Kalimdor's broader plains.

For a novice tauren hunter, completing initial rites in Mulgore is only the beginning. The lush valleys of their ancestral homeland are protected and familiar, nurturing beasts that test patience rather than sheer survival. Melor Stonehoof recognizes when a hunter's spirit has grown enough to require harsher trials. He instructs his pupils to pack their gear, leave the safety of Bloodhoof Village, and venture east across the mountain pass into the baked scrublands of the Barrens.

The path through the red rock canyons leads straight into the wide, sun-scorched savanna where the young Horde stakes its claim. At the intersection of Kalimdor's central trade routes lies the Crossroads, a fortified settlement bustling with orcs, trolls, and tauren. There waits Sergra Darkthorn, an experienced orc shaman renowned for her unforgiving standards. She acts as a mentor to any bold enough to stalk the Barrens' fierce fauna, promising to temper raw eagerness into hardened wilderness discipline.

The Hunter's Way is a rite of passage offered to aspiring trackers in Mulgore by the elder Skorn Whitecloud. To prove their emerging skill and respect for the wild, wanderers must fell the cunning flatland prowlers and present their claws to Melor Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise.

For the tauren, hunting is neither mere sport nor simple subsistence; it is considered one of their people's highest honors. It demands patience, awareness of the Earth Mother's balance, and reverence for the beasts that roam the rolling plains. Elder Skorn Whitecloud, resting in Mulgore after decades of tracking across Kalimdor, recognizes this restlessness in young adventurers. Rather than allowing them to wander aimlessly, he channels their ambition into a traditional trial of maturity and discipline.

To demonstrate that their tracking instincts are genuine, candidates are tasked with taking down Mulgore's flatland prowlers. These great cats are swift, stealthy, and cunning ambush predators that blend easily into the high grass of the plains. Gathering four sets of claws proves that a fledgling wanderer can spot a predator before becoming prey, turning the hunter's own ferocity back upon them.

Upon securing the trophies, the initiate ascends the soaring wooden towers and bridges leading up to Thunder Bluff. There, upon the Hunter Rise, Melor Stonehoof receives the claws. As a master tracker who values Skorn Whitecloud's ancient wisdom, Stonehoof accepts the offering as proof that the initiate possesses the right spirit to be guided further along the predatory paths of Kalimdor.

Dig Rat Stew is a culinary task offered by Grub, an orc camping east of the Crossroads in the Barrens. To satisfy a hearty desert appetite, Grub sends hungry adventurers south to the dwarven excavation at Bael Modan to gather a batch of plump dig rats for a dubious pot of stew.

Survival in the arid expanse of the Barrens demands an unpretentious palate. While seasoned hunters bring down zhevras, plainstriders, and raptors, the lone orc Grub has developed a peculiar craving for subterranean rodents. Claiming to be famished all day long, Grub promises to share his personal recipe with any traveler willing to do the undignified legwork of rat-catching.

The chosen source for these creatures is Bael Modan, the vast Alliance excavation site located deep in the southern Barrens. As dwarven prospectors tear into the red earth, their deep quarrying has inadvertently stirred up nests of prolific dig rats. While the dwarves view the tiny rodents as an infestation, Grub considers the overrunning critters an unmissable feast right under the enemy's nose.

Preparing Dig Rat Stew requires a sturdy stomach. According to Grub, the rodents are actually best when allowed to rot for several weeks to draw out their pungent taste. Though he settles for fresher specimens to satisfy a starving adventurer on the spot, his cooking techniques illustrate just how rough-hewn and forgiving roadside cuisine can be on Kalimdor's frontier.

The Escape is an escort quest in the northern Barrens where adventurers help the goblin pilot Wizzlecrank flee the Venture Company's drill site at the Sludge Fen. Trapped inside a stolen prototype shredder, Wizzlecrank requires protection against waves of company mercenaries until he clears the industrial pit. The mission concludes by reporting back to his contact, Sputtervalve, in the port town of Ratchet.

Having ignited the stolen prototype deep within the Sludge Fen drill site, Wizzlecrank quickly discovers that commandeering Venture Company engineering is easier said than done. With only a rudimentary grasp of the control levers and switches, the goblin lurches the heavy machine across the muddy quarry floor. His erratic driving and roaring mechanical joints inevitably alert nearby laborers and armed guards, turning what should have been a stealthy extraction into a chaotic running battle up the western ramp of the excavation pit.

The Venture Company does not take the theft of proprietary prototypes lightly. As the machine claws its way up the slope toward open ground, squads of company mercenaries deploy to intercept and disable the runaway construct. Despite the prototype lashing out to defend itself, the clumsy contraption cannot withstand concerted sabotage without outside bodyguard work. Clearing the rim allows the craft to stagger clear of the main drilling depression, though the machine suffers critical failure shortly thereafter.

Once out of the immediate danger zone, the prototype shredder breaks down entirely and collapses onto the savanna turf. Wizzlecrank scrambles out alive, instructing his rescuers to report to Sputtervalve in Ratchet while he stays behind with the wreckage. Sputtervalve, desperate to dissect the Venture Company's cutting-edge designs before his window of opportunity closes, immediately mobilizes a goblin salvage squad to haul whatever intact mechanisms survive back to port.
